subject.title: Model safety/alignment can block explicitly authorized operational tasks (e.g. SSH diagnostics)

question: Should OpenClaw define a trusted-operator/read-only diagnostics policy that can override generic model caution for authorized infrastructure tasks, and what boundary should it use?
rationale: The remaining work changes the model-safety/operator-authorization boundary and could affect provider routing and security posture; code inspection shows only narrower provider-refusal fixes today, not a settled product contract.

options.title: Design the operator-refusal contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open, settle the refusal taxonomy and read-only/destructive boundary, then land narrow implementation PRs under that policy.

options.title: Limit scope to provider-refusal failover
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98976 as the canonical narrow fix and leave trusted-admin behavior out of scope for now.

options.title: Sponsor an opt-in trusted-admin mode
options.body: Approve a new explicit config/policy knob for authorized read-only diagnostics, with security review and upgrade documentation before implementation.

recommendation.title: Design the operator-refusal contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, settle the refusal taxonomy and read-only/destructive boundary, then land narrow implementation PRs under that policy.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent provenance on Anthropic refusal fallback and model-fallback policy, and the issue is security/product sensitive.
